description:
FILED s515a (Opus, 2026-10-11) from Fable's review probe ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s513/review/p515a/iso-dup2.pl.  PRE-EXISTING (base and tree alike).
`open(my $f, ">&=", 1) or die; close $f; print "x\n";` -- perl keeps descriptor 1 open (an fdopen's close does not take the shared fd while STDOUT still holds it -- PerlIO refcounts the fd); PCL closes fd 1 and the program dies "Unable to flush stdout: Bad file descriptor".  #3185's %p-fdopen-alias covers the HANDLE forms (`>&=STDOUT`, `>&=`, $fh): the numeric form builds a fresh fd-stream on the SAME descriptor (%p-open-dup, `new-fd = src-fd` under eq-form), whose close closes the fd.  Fix direction: a numeric fdopen of a descriptor that a live handle already owns gets the alias of that handle's stream (or a stream whose close does not close the fd) -- probe `<&=0` and a non-standard fd too.


=== DONE (s518d, commit 1dd07695) ===
cl/pcl-runtime.lisp: (1) %p-open-dup's numeric `>&=N` / `<&=N` asks %p-stream-on-fd for a live handle's stream on descriptor N (the standard handles, the handle table, every open output stream -- a lexical handle) and aliases it (%p-fdopen-alias, as the handle forms do), so `close $f` leaves the descriptor open; (2) %p-close-previous-stream does not close a STANDARD handle still on its own descriptor at a reopen -- it flushes (perl keeps 0/1/2 across a reopen and dup2s onto them), so `open(STDOUT, ">&=1")` works (it was EBADF: the old fd 1 was closed first) and a FAILED reopen of STDOUT leaves it printing (probed 5.40.3: ok=0, print true, fileno 1; PCL closed STDOUT).  Probed vs perl: `>&=1` then close, `<&=0` then close, a non-standard fd of a lexical handle.  Guard Pl/t/tiehandle-01.t row 23, inverse-verified on main.  Note: the alias shares ONE buffer (the #3185 design), so with $| off perl's order across an fdopen of STDOUT can differ (perl `a c b d`, PCL `a b c d` -- scratch/s518d/pr/fd1.pl); not changed here.
subject: open(my $f, '>&=', 1); close $f closes descriptor 1 -- perl keeps it (the numeric fdopen form; the handle forms are #3185's alias)
